findings.title: Comment says unreported values render as "not reported", but the code renders "not computed"
findings.description: The comment above `system_prompt_mode` and `setting_sources` says a hand-built result with `None` "renders as 'not reported'". `_render_optional` in `review/persistence.py:317` returns the shared `_NOT_COMPUTED` sentinel, which is "not computed". The new test `test_unreported_values_render_the_shared_sentinel` asserts `- System prompt: not computed`. So the test and the code agree and the comment is wrong. Fix the comment, or define a single name for the sentinel and refer to it.

findings.title: Test helpers return `object`, which forces many `# type: ignore` comments in strict-checked tests
findings.description:
The Python rules include tests in strict pyright. `scripted_session`, `sdk_text`, `sdk_result`, `sdk_task_*`, `failing_reconnect_patch` and `typed_config` are all annotated as returning `object`. `typed_config` also takes a bare `type`. As a result, `tests/pipeline/test_sdk_session.py` is full of `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` on `session.dispatch(...)`, `session.background_tasks_waited`, `ledger.active` and similar. `_ledger_after` has the same problem. A blanket ignore also hides real attribute typos. `test_failed_reconnect_marks_session_unusable` already needs an `assert isinstance(session, SDKExecutionSession)` to narrow the type.

- Return `SDKExecutionSession` from `scripted_session`.
- Return `BackgroundLedger` from `_ledger_after`.
- Return `AssistantMessage`, `ResultMessage` and so on from the message builders.
- Return `AbstractContextManager[ScriptedClient]` from `failing_reconnect_patch`.
- Type `typed_config` as `Callable[..., object]`.

Then drop the ignores.

findings.title: Every SDK agent now gets an explicit `env`, and `base_env` is dead at this call site
findings.description:
The old code set `env` only when `setting_sources == []`. The new code always sets `kwargs["env"]`. Because `AgentConfig.auto_memory` defaults to `False`, any SDK agent built outside the pipeline paths, including `sq serve` agents with `setting_sources=None`, now runs with auto-memory disabled. The comment says this is a deliberate per-path choice, so I'm not flagging it as a bug. It is a behavior change for callers outside this slice's tests, so make sure that was intended.

Also, `base_env=kwargs.get("env")` can never return anything, because nothing sets `env` earlier in `create_agent`. The `# type: ignore[arg-type]` there is noise. Either remove the argument or keep it with a comment that it is a hook for a future env source.

findings.title: Rendering helpers and string constants now live in the data-model module
findings.description: `SystemPromptMode`, `describe_system_prompt`, `describe_setting_sources`, `describe_run_settings` and the `SETTING_SOURCES_*` display strings sit next to the Pydantic models. They are artifact and metadata rendering, not model definitions. `describe_system_prompt` also depends on the table in the `AgentConfig` comment ("the four rows of the table above"), so editing the model can silently invalidate the enum's docstring. A small `core/run_settings.py` would keep `models.py` to data definitions. It isn't urgent.

findings.title: The idle-timeout `except TimeoutError` is broader than the timer it guards
findings.description: While waiting on background agents, any `TimeoutError` that escapes `_read_turn_with_retry` is treated as the idle timeout. That includes one raised by the SDK or transport itself. The agents are then stopped and the partial text is returned as a normal result, with only a warning that says "no activity for Ns". In practice only `asyncio.timeout` should raise `TimeoutError` here, so this is low risk. Compare the elapsed time against `idle_s` before acting. Or catch the error inside `_read_turn`, where the timer is created, and re-raise it as a private subclass.

Test helpers return `object`, which forces many `# type: ignore` comments in strict-checked tests

Rendering helpers and string constants now live in the data-model module
